clue.text: Trial a head appears in is a case of some import

indicators.note: the phrase for 'per person' is said to show up inside the word for trial

parts.note: a trial is a test
a head means per person, or each, as in ten pounds a head

explanation.surface: A court hearing featuring a chief or headmaster turns out to be a legal matter of real significance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' is the pricing idiom for each, and 'appears in' places it inside TEST. 'Import' is not significance here but goods brought from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-style description: a wooden box in which leaves from India or China were shipped into Britain.

clue.text: Quivering sort of voice takes many in

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit it, so the voice word admits the numeral

parts.note: treble is the high singing voice of a boy
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, often clued as many

explanation.surface: A tremulous style of singing fools a great number of listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... in' wraps TREBLE round M. 'Quivering' is a noun here, a shake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: a shake or shudder, as in a quivering of the lip.

clue.text: Assailant's explosion of gross rage

definitions.note: the possessive 's is read as 'is', leaving the noun for one who attacks

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters of the two words after it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An attacker bursts out in a fit of ugly fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion of' rearranges GROSS RAGE. The OCR picked up stray words from a neighbouring column; the page prints only 'gross rage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who attacks first or without provocation.

clue.text: Lace centre has success, keeping on and on

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the word for success holds the first of the two short words

parts.note: a hit is a success, as a hit record is

explanation.surface: A lace-making business prospers by persevering year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short words are treated separately: 'keeping' tucks only the first inside the word for success. The answer is a Devon town in south-west England famous for its handmade lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual description: an English town in Devon renowned for its bobbin-made fabric.

clue.text: Tree-worship

definitions.meaning: the name of a European tree related to the rowan, with small pear-like fruit
a religious ceremony, as in morning worship at church

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a rowan-like tree bearing small fruit, and a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Chinese system getting Maoist extremely confused

indicators.note: thoroughly muddled, so the letters of the neighbouring word are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: China's political order leaves a follower of Chairman Mao thoroughly bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely confused' rearranges MAOIST. 'Extremely' tempts you to take outer letters, but it only intensifies the muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the philosophy and religion founded on the teachings of Lao Tzu is one of China's great belief traditions.

clue.text: Indication of grave situation in US city

definitions.meaning: a marker showing where a grave is situated
the Arizona city famous for the gunfight at the OK Corral

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a marker over a burial plot, and an Arizona frontier town.

clue.text: Vagabond no longer in shed

parts.note: someone no longer in is out
to shed something is to cast it off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: A tramp has stopped sleeping in the garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' is a verb here, not the hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a homeless wanderer rejected by society.

clue.text: Possible resort for Romans round end of June

definitions.text: Possible resort for Romans round end of June

indicators.note: round means going about, so the rearranged letters surround the single letter
resort read as re-sort, to sort again, so a possible new ordering of the next word's letters
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: People from Rome might holiday at this seaside spot as summer begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'Possible resort for' rearranges ROMANS to SANRMO, and 'round' wraps it about the E from 'end of' June.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual description: a seaside town on the Italian Riviera where people from the capital might holiday in early summer.

clue.text: Where power resides in dreadful regime? No, no!

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad state, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether authority lies with a tyrannical government and denies it emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges REGIME NO NO. The power in question is mechanical, not political.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: the part of a ship housing the machinery that drives it.

clue.text: HE keeps one in the shade

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the explosive holds the single letter

parts.note: HE abbreviates high explosive, of which TNT is the standard example
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A man makes sure that somebody stays out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'HE' is not a pronoun but the abbreviation for high explosive, giving TNT; 'keeps' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a slight colouring or hue of something.

clue.text: The speed of inspiration brings a chance to relax

parts.note: inspiration is the drawing in of breath, and 'of' makes it a possessive, adding an S
speed is pace

explanation.surface: The quickness with which a brilliant idea arrives lets the thinker put their feet up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The speed of inspiration' is read as a possessive phrase, the rate belonging to the act of inhaling, with the 'S run into the next word. Inspiration here is physical, not creative.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a pause in which one can rest and recover before carrying on.

clue.text: Points to dreadful scene — no accident, this

parts.note: points of the compass, here East and South

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad way, so the letters of the word beside it are disordered

explanation.surface: Evidence at a horrific site indicates that what happened was done on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges SCENE to SENCE. In philosophy an accident is a property a thing merely happens to have, the opposite of its fundamental nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Philosophical opposite: the intrinsic nature of a thing, as against its incidental properties.

clue.text: This fighter's no pro and not at all tough

parts.note: the opposite of pro, in pros and cons, is con
meat that is not at all tough is tender

explanation.surface: A boxer is described as an amateur and rather a softie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' suggests a professional but is the Latin for, whose opposite is against.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who competes for a title, especially in boxing.

clue.text: Jump on to one, taking part in game

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A child leaps on a playmate while joining in the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for the card game also called twenty-one or blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a card pastime in which players try to score twenty-one.

clue.text: Come to Nigeria for a change

indicators.note: a change alters things, so the letters of the two words before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit West Africa as a break from routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges TO NIGERIA. 'Come' is used as in 'to come from', to have a source.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: to arise or spring from a source, as in 'where does it come from?'.

clue.text: One may get fired from vehicle plant

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a bine is a climbing plant or its twining stem, such as the hop

explanation.surface: A worker could be sacked by a factory that builds motors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle plant' looks like one phrase for a factory but splits into two pieces; 'fired' means shot, not sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a short rifle is something that can be discharged.

clue.text: European country's courts holding us

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the word for courts contains the short word

parts.note: atria are the open central courts of Roman houses

explanation.surface: A continental nation's judges are keeping our group in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: The courts are architectural, the open halls of Roman houses, not legal ones; 'holding' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a landlocked Alpine republic in central Europe.

clue.text: Brideshead remained in ruins

parts.note: split into bride's head, the first letter of bride
something that remained lasted

explanation.surface: The great country house of Waugh's novel was left a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brideshead' must be split into 'bride's head'. Brideshead is the stately home in Evelyn Waugh's novel Brideshead Revisited.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: blighted or destroyed, as a heath or tree struck by lightning is.

clue.text: Making coffee for each ruler

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Someone brews a hot drink for every monarch present.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: brewing in a percolator, in the informal shortened verb.

clue.text: Not just imperfect

definitions.meaning: not fair or even-handed, favouring one side
incomplete, as in an eclipse that covers only some of the sun

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: biased towards one side, and incomplete.

clue.text: Runs over one box, loaded to the maximum

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first letter sits above the rest

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
one is I as a Roman numeral
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: A driver knocks into a single crate that has been packed completely full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' stacks R above I and CHEST in this down entry. 'Loaded' is slang for wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: loaded means wealthy, so the superlative is the most wealthy.

clue.text: Like race of reddish-yellow colour

definitions.meaning: a race is a root of the spice that flavours biscuits and beer, so this is resembling that root
having the sandy orange hue of the same spice, as some hair has

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: resembling a pungent spice root, and having its sandy orange hue.

clue.text: Order for actor — get inside, perhaps?

definitions.text: Order for actor — get inside, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the three words before it might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A director tells a player to go indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, with 'Enter' as the example in mind, and also the wordplay, 'perhaps' being the anagram signal; it first reads like a double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description with an example: a script's instruction to a performer, of which 'Enter' is the best known.

clue.text: One of us capturing rook with piece

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold, so the word for piece holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a piece of something is a bit
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A member of our chess team takes a castle using one of their men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of us' assumes the reader of The Times, a London newspaper, is British.
explanation.definitionFit: Example from the setter's viewpoint: an informal word for a native of the United Kingdom, as the paper's readers are presumed to be.

clue.text: Studied in modern centre, free

indicators.note: the centre of the word before it is its two middle letters

parts.note: to free someone is to liberate them

explanation.surface: Someone read for a degree at a new campus without paying fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' picks the middle letters of 'modern'. 'Studied' is an adjective here, as in a studied insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adjective: carefully considered and intentional, as a studied insult is.

clue.text: Lake is further round the bend

definitions.meaning: lake is a red pigment, and the best-known one is made from the root of this dye plant
round the bend is British slang for crazy, so further round it is crazier

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a red pigment from a dye plant, and the comparative of crazy.

clue.text: Bishop gets supply in a casual way

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
supply read as the adverb of supple, meaning in a lithe manner

explanation.surface: A churchman receives his provisions without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not provisions but the adverb from supple, pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in a carefree, unconcerned manner.
